text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Editorial says the government and the ruling Democratic Party should pay more attention to the phenomenon of pyramid schemes that is worrying the population.
- Police blocked about a thousand Albanians trying to reach the main Skanderbeg square to protest against a bankrupt pyramid scheme company Sude that still has their deposits.
- The Socialist Party's Tirana branch holds the second day of a meeting to discuss a confidence vote for the party's presidency and an extraordinary congress on recent developments in the party.
- While in Tirana Palestinian President Yasser Arafat rejected a U.S. State Department assessment that Israel had made some concessions on Hebron and the Palestinians should respond in kind.
- Tirana court ruled against Azem Hajdari's attempt to replace the present Independent Trade Union and its leader with his structures.
- Albanians are faced with the prospect of empty shops over Christmas and New Year because of the Greek farmers' blockade but still around 150 trucks left Albania for Greece.
- Hotel Tirana International, the biggest in the country, cannot pay back the last installment of about $1.1 million in credit received from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
- Albanian police forces have intensified checks of the seaside from air, land and sea to stop smuggling of illegal immigrants to Italy.
- The Socialist International forum will hold a meeting in Tirana.
- Exiled King Leka Zogu repeated the idea of a referendum to decide if Albania should be a republic or a monarchy.
- A widening budget deficit to 10 percent of the GDP and criticism from the International Monetary Fund may oblige the government to pass a provisional three-month budget for the coming year.
- The 35th song music festival started last night in Tirana.
